samples.summary: Notes read-only is enforced only at the CodeMirror layer; the `YorkieNoteStore` handed to the engine is never wrapped, so any write that does not go through a transaction still reaches the CRDT (docs has `read-only.ts` for exactly this)
samples.evidence: `new YorkieNoteStore(doc)` is constructed identically for a viewer and an editor mount (notes-view.tsx:136) and passed straight to `initialize(..., readOnly, ...)`. The new gate is `EditorState.changeFilter` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:453), which only sees CodeMirror transactions. This diff itself demonstrates the gap: `runHistory()` needed a separate hand-written `if (readOnly) return` (editor.ts:340) precisely because `store.undo()` writes straight to the CRDT without a transaction — i.e. the filter is not the chokepoint the comment claims, it is one of two chokepoints, and the second is a per-caller check. `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:35-45` documents why docs chose a *store*-level Proxy instead: 'the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one', and it deliberately allowlists readers so a member added tomorrow fails closed. `NoteStore` (packages/notes/src/store/store.ts:80-139) has 7 mutators today; the 8th added by a future change will forward to the CRDT on a viewer mount with nothing failing, while the design doc records the surface as 'inert by construction'. Attack: a viewer-role share link + any code path (existing `setLocalSelection`, a future mutator, or `EditorView.findFromDOM(el).state.facet(noteStoreFacet)` — `noteStoreFacet` is a public export of `@wafflebase/notes`, packages/notes/src/index.ts:29) writes to a document the link grants read-only.

samples.summary: The viewer read-only guarantee this change builds on has no server-side enforcement in the default configuration — the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode, so every gate added here is client-side only
samples.evidence: `this.enforce = configService.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101) defaults to false, and lines 111-119 then return ALLOW for a computed deny. `hasAccess()` would otherwise be the only thing refusing `link.role === 'viewer'` a write (line 217). Attack: a holder of a viewer-role share link calls `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (the frontend already does this at shared-document.tsx:959 and hands the result to the SDK), attaches with any Yorkie client outside the browser UI, and pushes arbitrary text ops to the note — no client-side `changeFilter`, `EditorState.readOnly` or `runHistory` guard is in the path. The diff's own comments (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:435-437, docs/design/notes/notes.md) acknowledge this, which makes it a known rollout state rather than a regression — but this change materially widens the surface that depends on it (a viewer is now given a live editor pane and the full `NoteEditorAPI` via the mounted toolbar), so it is worth restating that the boundary is unenforced by default. Mitigation is deployment-level (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`), not code.

samples.summary: The read-only decision is written fail-open: `role === "viewer"` means any role string that is not exactly `viewer` yields a fully editable mount plus a share-token image uploader
samples.evidence: `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer";` — `ResolvedShareLink.role` is typed `string` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:17), i.e. whatever the resolve endpoint returns. A value that is neither `viewer` nor `editor` (a new role such as `commenter`, a casing change, or a serialization slip) produces `readOnly === false`, which enables the whole formatting toolbar, the keymap picker, `EditorView.editable`, no `changeFilter`, and `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` at line 74. Today this is contained because `ShareLinkService.create` validates the role against `SHARE_LINK_ROLES` ('viewer'|'editor', share-link.service.ts:77) so no third value can be stored — hence minor rather than major. The fail-closed spelling (`resolved.role !== "editor"`) costs nothing and would keep a future third role read-only by default. Same shape exists in the pre-existing shared layouts, so this is a pattern note as much as a site note.

samples.summary: The new `changeFilter` is bypassable by design in CodeMirror — a transaction dispatched with `filter: false` skips change filters entirely, so the gate is not the absolute chokepoint the comment describes
samples.evidence: `EditorState.changeFilter.of(tr => Boolean(tr.annotation(Transaction.remote)))` is documented by CodeMirror as being consulted 'for each transaction (unless explicitly disabled)' — `TransactionSpec.filter: false` disables it. No first-party code in packages/notes dispatches with `filter: false` (I grepped), but third-party extensions in the mount do dispatch their own transactions (`@replit/codemirror-vim`, `basicSetup`'s autocomplete/search), and I could not verify their specs because node_modules is not installed in this checkout. Combined with the finding above (no store-level guard), a single extension that dispatches an unfiltered change on a read-only mount reaches `noteSync` → `store.editText()` → CRDT. Lowering confidence accordingly: I could not complete the chain to a concrete bypassing dispatch, only establish that the mechanism exists and is not defended against.

samples.summary: Mounting the toolbar for a viewer newly gives an anonymous share-link visitor a one-click 'Show authors' control, exposing every contributor's display name and edit timestamp
samples.evidence: `NotesToolbar` is rendered for `readOnly` visitors too, and the 'Show authors' checkbox sits in the view-mode dropdown *outside* the `!readOnly` guard (notes-toolbar.tsx:626 — only the keymap dropdown at line 549 is gated). Toggling it calls `setShowAuthors`, which reaches `NotesView`/`initialize` and paints `store.getAuthorSpans()` — display names of the workspace members who wrote each line, plus `at` timestamps (packages/notes/src/store/store.ts:36-49). Before this change the shared mount had no such control and fell back to the visitor's own stored preference, which defaults to false for an anonymous visitor (`readShowAuthors()` returns `read(key) === 'true'`, notes-settings.ts:47). The underlying names already travel to the client inside the CRDT content, so this is a UI-level disclosure of internal contributor identities to anyone holding a link rather than a new data leak — but it is a deliberate-looking product decision that no one appears to have made explicitly for the anonymous surface.

samples.summary: Letting a viewer switch into `edit` mode makes the editor pane focusable, which starts publishing that viewer's caret as a Yorkie presence write — a `doc.update` from a role that holds no write authority
samples.evidence: Previously the shared viewer mount was pinned to `viewMode="view"`, and `applyViewMode` sets `editorEl.style.display = 'none'` for that mode (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:504), so `update.view.hasFocus` could never be true and the live-caret publisher short-circuited. With the view menu the viewer can select 'Editor', focus the pane, and `noteRemoteSelections` then calls `store.setLocalSelection(anchor, head)` (remote-selection.ts:170), which reaches `this.doc.update((root, presence) => presence.set(...))` (yorkie-note-store.ts:436) — a real change pushed to the server. Two consequences: in the default shadow configuration a viewer-role link performs an (admittedly benign) document write; under `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` this is exactly the 'read-only client that still emits a local change' case docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:230-243 flags — yorkie derives the verb from the change pack, so the PushPull becomes `rw` and the webhook denies it, breaking the viewer's session. The change filter does not cover this path because it is not a document change. Low confidence: I could not confirm jsdom-free that a `contenteditable=false` CodeMirror content DOM takes focus on click, nor that Yorkie counts a presence-only change as `HasChanges()`.

samples.summary: Notes joins docs in giving anonymous editor-link holders an unauthenticated, unquota'd write into workspace image storage
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` posts to `POST /api/v1/shared/images`, whose only gate is a valid editor-role token (`assertCanWrite`, image-share-upload.controller.ts:129-143). The controller itself notes that 'a token still grants unbounded *cumulative* uploads for its lifetime' with only a 30/min throttle and a per-file Multer limit; an editor link that is shared publicly or leaked is therefore a durable anonymous upload credential into the workspace's key prefix. This is a pre-existing, explicitly deferred trade-off (docs already ships it) — flagged only because this change extends its blast radius to a second document type, and the design doc rewrites the former 'known limitation' wording without restating the quota gap.

verdict.reason: Verified the absence directly. `notes-view.tsx:136` constructs `new YorkieNoteStore(doc)` identically for viewer and editor mounts and passes it raw to `initialize(..., readOnly, ...)` (line 139); `editor.ts:474` installs that raw store as `noteStoreFacet.of(store)`. Read-only is enforced only at the CodeMirror layer (`EditorState.readOnly`, `EditorState.changeFilter` accepting only `Transaction.remote`, `EditorView.editable` — editor.ts:443-458), all of which see only transactions. There is no store-level guard anywhere: Glob of packages/notes/src shows no read-only module, and greps for `readOnlyNoteStore|readOnlyStore|Proxy(` across all packages find store proxies only in docs (`packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:74`, `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3218`), with `readOnlyDocStore` used only at `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075` and typed `DocStore` so it cannot wrap `NoteStore`. The gap is not hypothetical: `runHistory()` needs its own `if (readOnly) return` (editor.ts:340) with a comment saying undo/redo writes bypass the change filter, the vim path repeats the check differently (editor.ts:96-103), and `remote-selection.ts:170` calls `store.setLocalSelection()` unconditionally, which in `yorkie-note-store.ts:436` executes `this.doc.update(...)` — an actual CRDT write from a viewer mount past both gates. The client-side flag is the real boundary in a stock deployment because the Yorkie auth webhook defaults to shadow/allow-all (`documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185`, `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:200-205`), which is exactly the reasoning docs' own read-only.ts:35-45 records. In lane (access-control gate placed off the chokepoint, per-caller checks that fail open when a mutator is added), major severity, no counterexample found.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed evidence checks out verbatim. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 reads `configService.get<string>('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') === 'true'`, so an unset env var leaves `enforce === false`; lines 111-119 then convert any computed deny into HTTP 200 + `{allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}`. The viewer write refusal at line 217 (`return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`), reached from checkAttribute() line 181-182, is therefore never honored in the default configuration. The exploit chain is complete and in-tree: fetchYorkieShareToken() (frontend/src/api/auth.ts:187) POSTs a viewer share token to /auth/yorkie-token/share and returns a bare Yorkie token, which shared-document.tsx:959 feeds to the SDK's authTokenInjector; the same token can be used by any Yorkie client outside the browser, where the notes editor's client-side defenses (editor.ts:443 EditorState.readOnly, :454-456 changeFilter, :458 editable) are not in the path. I grepped all occurrences of YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE and found no deployment default setting it to true (no .env/compose/Dockerfile matches); self-hosting.md:185 and docs/design/sharing.md:208 both document the default as off/allow-everything, and the only code requiring true (template/seed/register-templates.ts:154, template-review.ts:80) gates the public template tier, not share links. So no guard elsewhere makes this unreachable. This is a missing/unenforced server-side authorization gate for share-link roles, which is squarely in the Security lens's access-control lane, and the code is exactly as described — I cannot refute on not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope grounds. The finding's own note that this is a known rollout state rather than a new regression bears on attribution, which is decided separately and is not a basis for refutation.
